result_text:
I changed the `all_files.zip` export in `DataExporter.java` so it builds the scope file names the same way the loose files are written. The `reports` module compiles and its tests pass (`mvn -q -o -pl reports test` printed no errors). I did not run the renamed-aspect scenario end to end.

**The change** (`reports/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporter.java`, `exportJson()`): the five hardcoded `aspect_*.txt` literals are replaced by a loop over the five scope aspects (main, test, generated, build and deployment, other). Each entry name comes from `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`, the same call `saveSourceCodeAspect` uses to write the loose file. The order is unchanged.

With the default config the entries are the same as before. With `buildAndDeployment` renamed, the fourth entry becomes `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`. `git-history.zip` was lost only because the exception aborted the same `try` block; with the lookup fixed it is written again when `git-history.txt` exists.

**Not changed:** `codeanalyzer/.../landscape/analysis/LandscapeAnalyzer.java` (around lines 280–284) has the same hardcoded `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt` literal. It reads the per-repository files for landscape reports, so a renamed aspect would also break that path. I left it alone because the task is scoped to the export. It is a good candidate for a follow-up.
